articles.title: Jovem fica cinco dias à espera de vaga em CTI após acidente de moto no Sul de MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Matheus Henrique Santos Vicente está internado desde domingo (18), em Varginha, após sofrer um forte impacto na cabeça. A transferência para um hospital em Divinópolis foi autorizada nesta sexta-feira (23).
articles.summary: Matheus Henrique Santos Vicente está internado desde domingo (18), em Varginha, após sofrer um forte impacto na cabeça. A transferência para um hospital em Divinópolis foi autorizada nesta sexta-feira (23).
articles.body:
Um jovem de 27 anos ficou cinco dias à espera de uma vaga em um Centro de Terapia Intensiva (CTI) após sofrer um acidente de motocicleta e bater a cabeça em Varginha (MG). Matheus Henrique Santos Vicente está internado desde domingo (18) no Hospital Bom Pastor. A transferência para o Hospital São João de Deus, em Divinópolis, no Centro-Oeste de Minas, foi autorizada na manhã desta sexta-feira (23), segundo a Secretaria de Estado de Saúde de Minas Gerais (SES-MG).

Durante os dias de espera, a família cobrou agilidade na transferência e demonstrou preocupação com a demora para conseguir um leito com suporte neurológico especializado.

“Desde domingo, a gente está aqui correndo atrás, com a zona de risco que o meu irmão está aqui, lutando pela vida. E está tendo um pouco de descaso aqui, cada vez fala uma coisa”, afirmou David Dário Vicente, irmão de Matheus.

O familiar também questionou a falta de informações claras sobre os critérios para a liberação da vaga e disse que a família não sabia mais a quem recorrer. “A gente está sem saber o que faz mais, quem a gente corre atrás, quem vai ajudar a gente”, desabafou.

Matheus Henrique Santos Vicente está internado desde domingo (18) no Hospital Bom Pastor, em Varginha (MG) — Foto: Reprodução EPTV

Segundo os familiares, Matheus sofreu o acidente em uma curva da Avenida Perimetral, nas proximidades da Fazenda Experimental, em Varginha. Ele teria perdido o controle da motocicleta durante a manobra, caído e sofrido um forte impacto na cabeça.

De acordo com os parentes, o capacete que o jovem usava chegou a se romper com a força da batida. Desde então, ele permanece na sala de emergência do Hospital Bom Pastor, sob cuidados médicos e monitoramento contínuo.

A equipe médica identificou a necessidade de transferência para um CTI com suporte neurológico especializado.

Em nota, a Secretaria de Estado de Saúde informou que a Central de Regulação de Leitos (CORE Saúde MG) realizou tentativas de transferência desde o primeiro dia de cadastro do paciente no sistema estadual.

Segundo a SES-MG, seis hospitais foram consultados: Hospital Regional do Sul de Minas, Hospital Universitário Alzira Velano, Santa Casa Paraíso, Santa Casa de Misericórdia de Lavras, Hospital das Clínicas Samuel Libânio e Hospital São João de Deus. De acordo com a secretaria, não havia leito adequado disponível nas unidades durante as tentativas anteriores.

O órgão explicou que a regulação considera a necessidade clínica do paciente, o perfil de atendimento exigido, as referências de assistência para cada região e a disponibilidade de leitos. A secretaria ressaltou que a prioridade é garantir o acesso ao serviço adequado em tempo oportuno.

Transporte será providenciado pelo hospital

A transferência de Matheus para o Hospital São João de Deus, em Divinópolis, foi autorizada na manhã desta sexta-feira (23). Segundo a SES-MG, o transporte deve ser providenciado pelo Hospital Bom Pastor, onde o jovem está internado.

Em posicionamento divulgado antes da autorização, a Fundação Hospitalar do Município de Varginha (FHOMUV), responsável pelo Hospital Bom Pastor, informou que o paciente recebia cuidados ininterruptos e monitoramento contínuo na sala de emergência.

A instituição afirmou que a solicitação havia sido cadastrada no sistema estadual e que a definição do hospital de destino dependia da regulação estadual do SUS.

A Secretaria Municipal de Saúde de Varginha informou que mantinha contato com a FHOMUV para contribuir com os encaminhamentos necessários à continuidade da assistência ao paciente, em articulação com a regulação estadual.

articles.title: Americana: motorista fica ferido ao bater carro contra muro de viaduto | G1
articles.standfirst: Homem de 42 anos foi socorrido e levado ao Hospital Municipal Doutor Waldemar Tebaldi após o acidente na manhã desta sexta-feira (23).
articles.summary: Homem de 42 anos foi socorrido e levado ao Hospital Municipal Doutor Waldemar Tebaldi após o acidente na manhã desta sexta-feira (23).
articles.body:
Motorista fica ferido após bater carro contra muro de viaduto em Americana — Foto: Guarda Municipal de Americana/Divulgação

Um motorista de 42 anos ficou ferido após bater o carro que dirigia contra o muro lateral do Viaduto Ministro Ralph Biasi , na região central de Americana (SP), na manhã desta sexta-feira (23).

Segundo a Guarda Municipal, o homem conduzia um veículo com placas de Santa Bárbara d’Oeste (SP), e trafegava no sentido da Avenida da Saudade. Ao entrar no viaduto, ele colidiu contra a estrutura .

Durante o atendimento da ocorrência, o motorista relatou aos guardas que não se lembrava das circunstâncias exatas que provocaram o acidente.

Ele não soube informar se teve a passagem fechada por outro veículo ou se perdeu o controle da direção. O airbag foi acionado e o homem relatou dores na região do peito abdômen.

Depois de receber os primeiros atendimentos no local, foi encaminhado ao Hospital Municipal Doutor Waldemar Tebaldi para avaliação e cuidados médicos.

A Guarda Municipal permaneceu no trecho do acidente para orientar os motoristas e sinalizar o trânsito na via.

articles.title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial
articles.summary: The scientists involved say the results could mark a turning point in cancer treatment, bringing personalised medicine a step closer.
articles.body:
A new personalised cancer vaccine given alongside a widely used immunotherapy drug has cut the risk of patients dying or their skin cancer returning by 42% in a major clinical trial.

The researchers involved say the results could mark a turning point in cancer treatment, bringing personalised medicine a step closer.

The trial also found that the new drug combination reduced the risk of melanoma, a type of skin cancer, spreading by 38% over two years compared to immunotherapy alone.

The drug manufacturers MSD and Moderna say the same approach is already being tested against other tumours, including kidney, bladder and lung cancer.

Independent cancer experts described the results as impressive but said longer-term studies were still needed to establish whether the treatment really helps most patients live longer, on average.

The new approach is aimed at cancer patients who have already had their tumour removed through surgery.

In the trial, 1,137 adults were given Keytruda, an established immunotherapy drug which helps the body's immune system find and attack cancer cells.

About two-thirds also received an experimental vaccine with the rest being given a placebo or dummy drug.

The vaccine, called Intismeran, uses the same mRNA technology as some Covid jabs.

It is personalised to each patient, using information from their own tumour to help train their immune system to recognise cancer cells and target them if they return.

Two years after starting the treatment, the patients who received the jab were far less likely to have had melanoma come back or see it spread across the body.

"Personalisation is the next step up and it's really exciting, it's a fabulous technology," says Prof Pippa Corrie, a consultant medical oncologist who helped run part of the study with patients at Addenbrooke's Hospital in Cambridge.

"The question is how much can we really demonstrate it's worth and this trial was the first proof of principle."

Prof Corrie worked with patients enrolled in the trial including 75-year old Tony Chapman, who was diagnosed with melanoma in 2019.

He had the tumour removed from his chest but a lump later appeared under his arm. He was told his cancer had returned and he needed a second operation.

He then volunteered to take part in the study but, like all the other participants, he still doesn't know whether he was given the experimental vaccine or a placebo alongside his immunotherapy treatment.

"This just seemed like a really good example of moving science forward, as well as getting some benefit for yourself, so what's to lose?" Tony said.

Three years on he is now having checks every six months and remains cancer-free.

Shares in the drugmakers MSD (known as Merck in the US) and Moderna have surged since both companies first hinted at the success of the vaccine in the summer.

But investors sold off stock on Thursday after financial analysts said the results were not quite as strong as those seen in an earlier, much smaller trial.

Both companies said they were now "engaging with authorities" suggesting they could file for approval from medicine regulators as soon as next year.

Widespread NHS use will also depend on cost, given that each individual patient will need to have their tumour genetically analysed and a personalised vaccine made for them.

The trial will continue so that the patients involved can be monitored – both to see if the cancer returns over time and to assess whether the drug ultimately helps them live longer.

Professor Alan Melcher from the Institute of Cancer Research in London, who wasn't involved in the research, described the results as "very impressive".

"It is an important proof of principle for the field, although we shouldn't get ahead of the evidence," he said.

"We can't assume from one melanoma trial that the same approach will work across all cancers, and longer follow-up will be important to understand the effect on overall survival."

The full trial results are due to be presented at the European Society of Medical Oncology (ESMO) cancer conference in Madrid on Saturday.

They have yet to be published in a peer-reviewed medical journal, where they can be scrutinised by independent experts.

articles.title: Second autopsy after woman lawyer’s death in locked flat raises family’s doubts
articles.summary: Second autopsy held after Hazaribag lawyer Anushka Chakraborty found hanging in locked flat; family disputes suicide, alleges harassment; police probe code lock.
articles.body: Hazaribag: A second post-mortem examination was conducted on Friday on the body of 28-year-old Anushka Chakraborty, a day after the lawyer was found hanging inside the room of her apartment in Hazaribag’s Bengali Colony, as her family refused to accept the death as a suicide and demanded a deeper probe.Anushka’s body was found around 10 am on Thursday in the apartment, which falls under Bada Bazar police station limits. Police have seized electronic devices and are examining the sequence of events before her death, including how and when the flat’s electronic code lock was activated.Her brother, Devjit Chakraborty, has raised questions over a message reportedly sent to their mother before the death. He said Anushka usually communicated with her mother through calls or voice notes and, whenever she texted, wrote in Bengali. The final message, however, was typed in Hindi.The message reportedly said: “Mom, please forgive me, but I cannot bear this anymore. I know I cannot come back home. My husband himself told me that only my corpse will leave from here, so this is for the best. I will not be able to live. I am completely exhausted now. I just can’t do this anymore. Sorry, Mom.”Devjit alleged that Anushka had suffered a miscarriage days earlier and was later taunted and mentally harassed by her husband, Kushagra Rudra, and her in-laws over her inability to bear a child. Police have not independently established the allegations, which remain under investigation.The family has also pointed to photographs and videos from Sindoor Khela celebrations on Wednesday, saying Anushka appeared happy hours before her death.Bada Bazar police station officer in-charge Mukesh Kumar Rajak said police were looking for Rudra, who had not returned to Hazaribag even 24 hours after the incident. Police said Rudra called emergency number 100 but did not come to the apartment. When contacted, he reportedly said he was in Palamu and would return soon.Police entered the flat with help from Rudra’s driver. Investigators are now trying to determine who locked the apartment and when. Anushka’s parents have demanded justice. Ramgarh MLA Mamta Devi met the family at Sadar Hospital.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Jersey's health spending on Southampton taxis surges by 75%
articles.summary: It comes as the department looks to review spending for off-island hospital treatment.
articles.body:
The amount of money spent on taxis for Jersey patients visiting Southampton hospital and the surrounding area has risen by 75% in two years.

In 2023, £140,594 was spent on taxi provision, which surged to £246,542 in 2025.

Islanders can request a taxi if it is "not possible or practical" to use public transport, or if there is a "medical reason" to do so.

The Health department has been asked for comment.

The government's patient travel policy states that travel from a port to a UK hospital should be on services contracted by Health and Care Jersey.

Were that was not possible, "patients should use public transport and pay for this themselves" and have the costs reimbursed by the Travel Office.

It also said that where there was a "medical reason", or it was not "possible or practical" to use other means, "the Travel Office could consider and, if necessary, pre-book a taxi or hire car as appropriate".

In a Freedom Of Information (FOI) request , Health & Care Jersey published the amount of money spent on taxis over the last three years.

It showed that spending has risen by just over 75% since 2023:

Health and Care Jersey said the figures cover travel in areas around Southampton and "cannot be considered representative of expenditure on taxis for patients attending Southampton hospital alone".

It comes as patient travel costs are being reviewed, after being described as "very generous" by a Health Board leader.

Following that intervention, Health Minister Tom Binet said he would consider whether "UK travel should continue to be paid for all patients in all circumstances".

He said: "The health budget is under growing pressure...[and] it is essential that all our resources are used in the most effective way".

"Officers are actively working to ensure that the costs we currently pay...represent value for money".

The health department has been approached for further comment.

articles.title: Man, 100, and Wife, 99, Share 6 Tips for a Long Life and Their ‘Secret Weapon’ for Longevity
articles.summary: 100-year-old Bernie Gerson and his wife Eleanor have been married 80 years. They share their longevity tips, crediting this breakfast food and healthy habits.
articles.body: Eleanor and Bernie Gerson marked their 80th wedding anniversary this year, but there’s so much more to celebrate. He’ll be 101 years old in November; she’ll turn 100 in January. They met as teenagers but went their separate ways until “destiny” brought them back together, he says. The couple lives independently with the help of their daughter who resides with them in Warrington, Pennsylvania. “We are very, very thankful for still being together,” Bernie Gerson tells TODAY.com. His wife is still amazed by their whirlwind marriage, which came after he proposed via letter while serving on a U.S. Navy warship in the Pacific during World War II. “Now I look back at it, I realize how young we really were, and how much we have had to find out about life,” Eleanor Gerson says. He drove a car and played tennis until his 90s, and has a “secret weapon” when it comes to his diet. She always liked to be active, walking, volunteering and helping others. “I feel that having each other has kept them going this long,” their granddaughter, Allison Snyder, tells TODAY.com. She likes to describe her grandparents as “peanut butter and jelly” because they’re inseparable. Their daughter, Renee Gerson, 79, believes healthy eating, exercise and always being involved in the community have been important factors. Here are the couple’s simple tips for a long life: Eat a Healthy Diet Both credit wheat germ, which they’ve been eating for as long as they can remember, for their longevity, Snyder says. Bernie Gerson sprinkles a heaping tablespoon of wheat germ on his cereal every morning, calling it his “secret weapon” for good health and smooth skin. “Nobody takes me for my age because I don’t look like a lot of people who are 101,” he says. Wheat germ is the “healthiest part of the wheat kernel,” according to the University of California, Davis. It’s a “unique source of concentrated nutrients,” researchers note, and is rich in bioactive components with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, studies have found. It’s also a good source of “anti‐aging polyamines,” compounds that can play a role in preventing chronic diseases. Bernie Gerson’s daily morning meal of cereal with wheat germ and milk also includes crushed walnuts, sliced almonds, blueberries, strawberries and a banana. Eleanor Gerson eats oatmeal with blueberries, honey and cinnamon for breakfast. She also likes berries and apples, which are among the healthiest fruits. Both love cinnamon buns and pastries with their coffee, but keep the portions small. The couple usually skips lunch and has a variety of foods for dinner, including eggplant parmesan, fish, grilled cheese, pasta or eggs. They don’t drink alcohol. Stay at a Healthy Weight The Gersons made an effort to avoid weight creep, or the tendency to gain weight as people age. It can lead to obesity and increase the risk of heart disease and other chronic illnesses, studies have found. “I always watched my weight through the years, and my wife does, too,” Bernie Gerson says. “We’ve never been heavy in our whole life.” He loves chocolate, for example, but holds himself back — enjoying just a little taste. The centenarian still wears the same size suit he wore when he was a young adult. Be Active Eleanor Gerson introduced her husband to tennis by signing them both up for lessons and “created a monster,” she jokes. He was reluctant to go at first, but got hooked on it immediately and played until he was 94. Some doctors believe tennis is the healthiest sport because it’s a whole-body workout. Bernie Gerson also played basketball, football and baseball, and took up jogging when few other people were running. “Being healthy and in shape was a very important thing in my life,” he says. Eleanor Gerson shared that goal. “I always liked to be active. I enjoyed that, and I think that makes a happy person,” she notes. She regularly walked and played tennis for a while. Laugh and Talk “We like to laugh a lot, Ellie and I. I think that keeps you young and keeps your mind in good shape,” Bernie Gerson says. His granddaughter calls him a “naturally happy person” who likes to tell jokes. Her grandmother is the conversationalist. The couple enjoys discussing current events and politics at dinner together every evening, Snyder notes. Bernie Gerson’s No. 1 rule for couples is to never go to bed mad. “You should stay up all night and fight,” he says. “Always have respect for one another and admire your spouse.” Love Deeply The Pennsylvania couple met in 1941 when both their families were vacationing in Atlantic City and stayed next door to each other. He was not quite 16, she was 14. “I used to see her go to the beach, and I’d say, ‘She’s so pretty, I would love to meet her,’” Bernie Gerson recalls. They did meet on the boardwalk when he asked a mutual friend to introduce them. He jotted down her phone number, but they didn’t stay in touch when she went back to Philadelphia and he to Norristown. About two years later, Bernie Gerson was on a date with another girl in Philadelphia when he spotted Eleanor with her date at a dance. He called her the next day. Bumping into her again was “destiny,” the centenarian believes. Bernie Gerson proposed marriage in a letter while serving in the U.S. Navy on board the USS Wilkes-Barre during World War II. The Purple Heart recipient was at sea in the Pacific Ocean, so it took months for him to find out she accepted. When he came home, she told him, “You’re under no obligation. We don’t really know each other that well.” But she was willing to go with it, she says. “We’re getting married,” he replied. The wedding took place nine weeks later on July 14, 1946. Stay Positive Bernie Gerson says his father told him at an early age that he should have “good MA,” or mental attitude. “He’s so right. If you think positive, it’s a wonderful gift,” Gerson says. “It’s easy to be negative and talk bad about things, but if you have a good MA, you can almost overcome anything that happens to you.”

articles.title: Craig Melvin Jokes This 1 Trendy Workout Helped Him Nab People’s Sexiest Morning Show Host
articles.summary: Craig Melvin reveals the workout that helped him win the morning host category in People’s Sexiest Man Alive Readers’ Choice poll and the benefits of Pilates.
articles.body: Craig Melvin didn’t reach “Sexiest Man Alive” status just by sitting on the couch — he had help from a famous workout. The TODAY co-anchor recently won the “hotter than your cup of coffee” morning host category in the People’s Sexiest Man Alive Readers’ Choice poll. It may have helped that Savannah Guthrie encouraged viewers to “vote early and often” after he was nominated last month. But guests on the show also couldn’t resist asking Craig about how he accomplished the feat and stays in shape. “Tell us what you did, I think people want to know,” NBC News medical contributor Dr. Akshay Syal teasingly inquired during a segment about exercise goals for every age on Friday, Oct. 23. The inquiry prompted laughter from TODAY’s Dylan Dreyer and Laura Jarrett. “Pilates — a lot of Pilates, because I was having issues with my back and my core,” Craig answered. “You too can win the award if you do Pilates,” Syal jokingly told the viewers. Pilates, named after founder Joseph Pilates, focuses on exercises to strengthen and tone the core — which includes the abs, back, hips and glutes — plus the arms and legs, explains TODAY Fitness contributor Stephanie Mansour, a certified personal trainer and a yoga and Pilates instructor. Repeated movements work the midsection, which can be especially beneficial for people with back problems, she adds. The low-impact workout helped to cure her chronic back pain. Pilates can be done on a mat or a reformer machine. When Craig previously tried the machine version, he called it “perhaps the most intense” workout he’d ever done, noting that it left him sore for three days afterward. Mansour recommends these 20 simple Pilates exercises for beginners to strengthen the core, relieve back pain and flatten the stomach.

articles.title: Chhawla tank victims entered confined space without protective gear: cops
articles.summary: Delhi Chhawla septic/water tank death: Police say 4 men entered confined space without safety gear; 1 dead, 3 hospitalised; negligence case filed.
articles.body: New Delhi: Delhi Police, probing the death of a man at an under-construction septic/water tank in southwest Delhi’s Chhawla on Oct 21, have found that he and three others, who fell sick after inhaling toxic fumes, had entered the tank without wearing protective safety gear.A preliminary inquiry revealed that the incident occurred inside an under-construction water/septic tank on a residential plot. Police said the tank did not contain sewage or water at the time. The four men had allegedly entered the confined space to remove shuttering and inspect construction work when they inhaled toxic gases.According to investigators, a contractor, identified as Madan Pandit (38), entered the tank after labourer Vinod (22) climbed inside and stopped responding. Pandit went down to check on him. When neither of the two emerged, the plot owner’s sons, Chander Shekhar (35) and Surender Singh (42), allegedly entered the tank in an attempt to rescue them but fell sick after inhaling toxic fumes. Pandit was taken to a hospital, where he was declared dead on arrival. The three others are undergoing treatment, said police.Police said a mobile crime team inspected the spot and photographed the scene. Pandit’s body was shifted to the mortuary at RTRM Hospital for post-mortem and other legal formalities.A case of negligence has been registered, and police are investigating whether the construction work had the necessary permissions and whether any safety lapses contributed to the incident. No arrests have been made so far.The incident is the latest in a series of deaths linked to toxic gases in confined spaces in Delhi. In June this year, three men died after inhaling toxic fumes inside a septic tank at a factory in Mundka Industrial Area. In May 2025, a man died after entering a septic tank at a house in New Ashok Nagar, while another person was injured during a rescue attempt. articles.title: NHRC seeks cop action on plaint over Hailakandi schoolgirl gang rape-murder within 8 weeks
articles.summary: NHRC directs Hailakandi police to act in 8 weeks on complaint over alleged gang rape-murder of 15-year-old; JJB recommends 16-year-old be tried as adult.
articles.body: Silchar: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has directed Hailakandi police to act within eight weeks on a complaint over the alleged gang rape and murder of a 15-year-old schoolgirl.The directive followed a complaint filed by Delhi-based social activist Krishna Rajput through HRCNet portal on Sept 2. The complaint sought a fair, time-bound investigation and accountability for any lapses by public authorities.According to NHRC’s action-taken record dated Oct 19, the complaint was disposed of with directions and forwarded to the Hailakandi SP for appropriate action within eight weeks. The police have also been asked to inform the complainant of the action taken.The complaint raised concerns over alleged violations of the victim’s right to life, dignity and bodily integrity, and sought the preservation of medical and forensic evidence. It also called for an examination of possible negligence or dereliction of duty by public officials and action against those found responsible.NHRC’s directive comes amid developments in the criminal proceedings. Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) in Hailakandi has recommended that a 16-year-old accused be considered for trial as an adult following a preliminary assessment under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act.The order was passed by the board’s principal magistrate after considering the alleged offence, psychological assessment reports from Silchar Medical College and Hospital, and a report submitted by the investigating officer.Under the Juvenile Justice Act, children aged 16 to 18 accused of heinous offences may undergo a preliminary assessment to determine whether they should face trial as adults. The final decision rests with the Children’s Court, which will examine the matter independently. The assessment does not establish the juvenile’s guilt.The special investigation team (SIT) earlier filed a chargesheet against five accused, including four adults and the juvenile. The investigation involved forensic evidence, medico-legal reports, digital records, witness statements and seized materials.The chargesheet was filed under Section 193 of the BNSS. The case was initially registered under Sections 65(1) and 103(1) of the BNS, read with Section 6 of the Pocso Act. Police later invoked additional provisions of the BNS.According to police, the schoolgirl was found in a bloodied condition inside her residence on the night of Aug 1 while her family members were attending a social event. Police began investigating after receiving information about the incident, and forensic experts collected evidence from the scene.Five accused were arrested in connection with the case. The juvenile’s identity has been withheld in accordance with the law.The incident triggered protests across Hailakandi district, with residents, women’s organisations and civil society groups demanding stringent punishment and speedy justice for the victim’s family.The NHRC complaint is separate from the criminal proceedings and concerns accountability for the authorities’ handling of the case.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Guwahati | Silver Rate in Guwahati | Bank Holidays in Guwahati | Public Holidays in Guwahati | Guwahati AQI | Weather in Guwahati | Petrol Price in Guwahati | Diesel Price in Guwahati | CNG Price in Guwahati | LPG Price in GuwahatiStay updated with the latest Guwahati news. articles.title: Student killed in wall collapse due to heavy rain;  southern TN braces for more
articles.summary: Heavy rains in southern Tamil Nadu kill 17-year-old in Virudhunagar, damage homes, disrupt Kodaikanal traffic; red alert issued for hill districts.
articles.body: Madurai: Heavy rains across southern Tamil Nadu left a Class XII student dead in Sattur in Virudhunagar district, damaged several houses, temporarily cut off roads to Kodaikanal and caused check dams to overflow on Friday. Flooding also forced restrictions at popular waterfalls, while rising reservoir levels prompted warnings to riverside communities.S Muthuselvi, 17, died after a wall collapsed inside her family’s tiled-roof house at Mettamalai near Sattur in Virudhunagar district around 11pm Thursday. The family was asleep when the central wall gave way following hours of rain. Her mother, Solaiammal, suffered a leg fracture. Neighbours pulled them from the debris and took them to Sattur govt hospital, where the girl died on Friday morning.The student attended Government Higher Secondary School in Chinnakamanpatti. Her father, Selvam, a daily wage worker, escaped injury. Social welfare minister K Jegadeshwari visited the hospital on Friday, handed the family Rs4 lakh in govt relief and assured assistance to construct a new house. Police registered a case.In M Vellalapatti near Melur, roofs of five houses collapsed and four others were partly damaged, but residents escaped injury after vacating the buildings. Elsewhere, an 85-year-old woman was injured by a falling wall in Thoothukudi, three houses were damaged near Kayathar, and a farmer’s house was destroyed at Kovilankulam in Ramanathapuram district.Meanwhile, floodwater near Shenbaganur disrupted access to Kodaikanal, leaving tourist cars and buses stranded for nearly two hours on Friday. Dindigul collector advised tourists against travelling to Kodaikanal due to landslides, fallen trees and flooding along access roads. Tourists were also barred from bathing at Kumbakkarai in Theni, Thiruparappu in Kanniyakumari and major Courtallam waterfalls in Tenkasi, where swollen streams made entry unsafe.In Theni, where Thekkady recorded 7.5cm of rain, the Anaipillaiyar check dam near Bodi overflowed, while Sothuparai reservoir reached its full level of 126.28 feet, releasing excess water into the Varaha river. Vaigai and Mullaperiyar reservoirs rose to 46.52 feet and 119.75 feet, respectively, prompting authorities to warn people against entering swollen rivers or crossing flooded stretches.The weather department issued a red alert for extremely heavy rain in the hill areas of Tirunelveli and Kanyakumari on Friday. Very heavy rain is forecast there and in Theni on Saturday, with Madurai and neighbouring districts facing further downpours on Sunday.
